title: Position index of a filtered tagged list stays below the length bound
statement: Let $t$ be a finite list of elements of a type $\alpha$, and tag each entry of $t$ with its position to form the list of pairs $(t_i, i)$, whose second coordinates run through $0, 1, \dots, |t| - 1$. Let $p$ be any Boolean predicate on such pairs, and let $w$ be a natural number with $|t| \le w$. If a pair $(l, \mathit{idx})$ occurs in the sublist obtained by keeping exactly those tagged pairs on which $p$ is true, then $\mathit{idx} < w$.
hypotheses_covered: t is a list over α, tagged with positional indices
p is a Boolean predicate on element–index pairs
(l, idx) belongs to the filtered tagged list
the length of t is at most w
replaced:
If $(l, \mathit{idx})$ arises from filtering $t.\mathrm{zipIdx}$ by a predicate and $t$ has
length at most $w$, then $\mathit{idx} < w$.
